chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hakam, from al-Husayn ibn Saif ibn 'Amirah, from Hisham ibn Salim, who said:

I heard Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) saying: 'Whoever says “La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah al-'Ali al-'Azeem”, Allah, the Mighty and Sublime, will remove from him seventy types of calamities, the least of which is suffocation.'

key_terms.الْعَلِيِّ الْعَظِيمِ: The Most High, The Most Great
key_terms.لَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّه: There is no power and no strength except with Allah

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for reciting La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah al-Ali al-Azeem?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-A'mal*, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) highlights the profound protective power of the phrase 'La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah al-'Ali al-'Azeem', promising deliverance from seventy distinct types of calamities. The inclusion of 'al-'Ali al-'Azeem' (the Most High, the Greatest) emphasizes that divine protection stems from Allah’s supreme authority and majesty, making this dhikr a comprehensive shield against both minor and severe trials, with suffocation cited as the least severe affliction removed.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1.  It is narrated that Imam Ja’far Sadiq (a.s.) said, “Allah, the Mighty and Sublime will remove seventy types of calamities from  the  one  who says  ‘Laa  h’aula  wa  laa  quwwata  illaa billaahil a’liyyil a’z’eem’ the least of which is death due to suffocation.”
